message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. A few years ago, I was renting a place with this dude. We were on a lease, and when the lease was ending, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, leaving only the last bit of his half of the rent and a few things he didn't want to bring with him. There was a note saying he didn't want those things. Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and that cost comes out of your deposit. I've heard of people losing $250 just because someone had to take three milk crates of stuff to the dump. That's a rip-off. So, I tried to contact him for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump. But he never responded. I ended up taking most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I thought, "Why not sell them?" There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Fast forward to last week, I was at a party where he was also present. We were being polite, and then he asked how the move-out process went. I told him it was good, and naturally, he asked what I did with his stuff. When he found out I sold his games, he got mad. I told him I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now, he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing wrong with what I did. But now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for selling his games without his permission. Okay, so to break this down, I need to consider a few things: 1. **Communication**: Did I make reasonable efforts to contact him before selling his stuff? 2. **Ownership**: Did I have the right to sell his games, or were they still his property? 3. **Intentions**: Was my intention to cause harm, or was it to prevent financial loss? 4. **Ethics vs. Legality**: Just because something is legal, does that mean it's morally right? 5. **Consequences**: How has this affected our relationship, and is that a factor in determining if I'm the asshole? Starting with communication, I did try to contact him for two weeks. That seems reasonable. But maybe I could have tried more methods, like calling him or visiting his new place if I knew where he was. However, I don't know if that's practical or possible. Next, ownership. The games were his property, even though he left them behind. By law, I might have had the right to dispose of them, but ethically, selling them without his consent might be crossing a line. I mean, I could have donated them or stored them safely until he could pick them up. Intentions-wise, I didn't sell the games to harm him. My intention was to prevent the landlord from charging me for removing his stuff, which could have cost me money. But by selling the games, I actually made money, which might make it seem like I was taking advantage of the situation. Ethics vs. Legality: Legally, I might be in the clear, but ethically, there's a gray area. Selling someone's belongings without their permission, even if it's to prevent a financial loss, can be seen as disrespectful or exploitative. Consequences: Our relationship has been affected negatively. He's upset and calling me names. That's a significant consequence, and it makes me wonder if it was worth it to sell the games for $600, especially if it caused such harm. I also need to consider if there were alternatives. Could I have stored the games somewhere safe until he could pick them up? Or maybe donated them to a charity or sold them and given the money to him? That might have been a better approach. In the end, while I might not be legally in the wrong, ethically, there's a case to be made that I acted in a way that disrespected his ownership and caused unnecessary harm to our relationship.
